**Finding: Deviation (medium severity) — Section 13, paragraph p0047**

**What I found.** The document has no dedicated personnel section, but a non-solicit does exist, tucked into the run of miscellaneous provisions numbered under § 7: Section 13 "NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES."

**Direction and scope analysis:**

| Element | Contract terms | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Who is bound | "Neither party" — binds us too | Preferred: no non-solicit on Customer |
| Scope | Only personnel with "direct involvement with the Services" | ✅ Matches fallback |
| Duration | 1 year post-termination | ✅ Inside 24-month walk-away |
| No-hire? | "solicit for hire" — solicitation-based only | ✅ No flat no-hire |
| General-ad carve-out | **Absent** | ❌ Required by fallback |

**Assessment.** Because the clause binds Clear Capital, the preferred position (no non-solicit on us) is not met. But the clause is already mutual, already narrowed to Services-involved personnel, already short-dated, and is not a no-hire — so it is close to our fallback and outright deletion would be disproportionate to the existing bargain. The one genuine gap is the missing carve-out: as drafted, an ordinary job posting or an inbound candidate who left RadialSpark could technically put us in breach, and the consent gate ("not unreasonably withheld") is thin protection.

**Redline (fallback, validated ok:true).** Appended a carve-out sentence permitting (a) general advertisements, postings and recruiting not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, including general search-firm efforts, and (b) hiring individuals who approach unsolicited or respond to such general efforts. Mutual, so it reads as even-handed and should be an easy ask.

I left duration untouched — the fallback measures 12 months from the end of involvement rather than from termination, but the difference is marginal here and not worth spending negotiating capital on. Confidence: 0.83.
